title: Run a pretend shop: price three things you made
description: Drawings, pebble pets, paper planes — a pretend shop turns your own creations into stock, and forces the first real question of every business: what should this cost?
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Stock and price tags
paragraphs: Make or choose three things to sell and give each a price tag. Pricing is the game: too dear and the shopkeeper's family-customers walk past; too cheap and the till is empty by closing time. Think about what each thing cost you in time and materials.
Write the prices in real money amounts and set out play money or drawn notes for change. Making change correctly is where pretend shops quietly teach real arithmetic.

body.heading: Open for trading
paragraphs: Invite customers, take turns being shopkeeper and buyer, and haggle politely. At closing time, count the till together: which price worked, which was too high, and what would you change tomorrow?
That closing count is the lesson real shops learn from too: prices are not wishes, they are experiments — and every experiment teaches something.

takeaway: Price three homemade things, trade with play money, make real change, then count the till: prices are experiments, and the closing count is the lesson.
materials: Paper price tags and a pencil
Play money or drawn notes and coins
A box or tray for a till
supervision: Play money only — no real money, cards or accounts are used in this game.
safetyNotes: Use pretend prices and play money throughout; never real payment details.
Small coins of play money should be kept away from very young children.
